profile: PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2 with the registered search path and native parameter style.
scope: IS DISTINCT FROM and IS NOT DISTINCT FROM over pure int4 leaves and SQL NULL.

Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.role: A non-null Boolean test of equality or difference treating NULL as comparable.
Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.structure: Two ordered signed int4 column, signed literal or NULL operands and the requested equality polarity.
Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.conditions: The enclosing scope checks both references and counts both operands. Analyze only checked int4 leaves and NULL in the registered catalog-first profile. Bare NULL can be tested without an equality overload on its own.
Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.meaning: Two NULLs are equal. Exactly one NULL is different. Compare two nonnull int4 values using pg_catalog equality. The selected polarity determines the Boolean result. A WHERE filter admits true rows only.
Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.externalInterpretation: Read the same referenced physical slots using the fixed int4 domain. A competing operator in an earlier runtime schema cannot change the built-in equality.
Predicate/IntegerDistinctness.sql: Use COALESCE of the qualified nullable equality and the conjunction of both IS NULL tests. Emit NOT for the distinct polarity. Write each NULL operand as pg_catalog.int4.

observations: Exact Boolean metadata and labels, equal and different nonnull values, both NULL, left or right NULL, duplicate rows and filtering.
A real earlier schema overload of int4 equality must produce a different result when selected. Compare the same emitted value under that runtime search path.

finite.identity: Every pair of ordered operands, both polarities and both placements. Source-free units omit slots. Require each of the 236 observed identities exactly once per release.

exploration.structure: Vary signed boundary values, NULL operand positions and binding slots. Vary row multiplicity, result widths and repeated labels. Compose with logical decisions, CASE and NULL tests.
